title: Discovered attacks and checks

D0.outcome: Describes a discovered attack (moving one piece uncovers a line of another) and says why the moving piece is free to make a second threat.

D1.outcome: When told 'find the discovered check or attack', finds the masking-piece move that uncovers it and says what the moved piece attacks.

D2.outcome: In mixed sets, finds the discovered attack that wins material or mates, and does not play it when the opponent's reply captures the uncovering piece or blocks the line.

D3.outcome: Chooses the best move for the masking piece (capture, strongest threat, or the move that sets up a see-saw) and checks that the uncovered line cannot be interposed.

misconceptions: The moving piece must have a harmless job; it can attack or capture anything.
A discovered check always wins material.
conditions: A discovered check is a pin in which the pinned piece has changed sides: the masking piece can capture anything, attack anything or relocate, and cannot be recaptured because the opponent is in check.
It works best against a king with few flight squares.
The see-saw: a piece that checks from one square and discovers a check from another wins material with every swing because the king has only one move.
contrasts: A discovered attack on a non-king target, which the opponent answers with a counter-threat or by moving the target with a gain of tempo.
The discovered line can be interposed by a piece that also attacks the masking piece.
The masking piece's departure uncovers a line to a square where nothing of the opponent stands.

soft_prereq_notes.TAC.PIN.D1: a discovered check is a pin in which the pinned piece has changed sides (Nimz #29)
soft_prereq_notes.TAC.FORK.D1: the masking piece usually makes a second threat, as in a fork
